text:
Lucas Raymond is a point-a-game player again, 21 points in 21 games, and the Red Wings lean on him in every way they can: nearly 20 minutes a night and 10 of those points on the power play. Since Dylan Larkin stopped playing to wait out a trade, the Wings have struggled, losing six of seven at one point, and Raymond has kept producing anyway, with a point in eight of his last ten games.

The good news for anyone wondering if it's real: it is. His shooting sits right around league average and his goals match the quality of his chances almost exactly. Our talent range puts his scoring rate between 2.5 and 3.3 points per 60, and his current 3.0 sits in the middle of it.

He's a setup man first. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.7 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 87th percentile among forwards, and Evolving-Hockey had him 26th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement while drawing the other team's best. Watch where the puck goes after he gets it on the half wall. The shot usually belongs to someone else, and the assist to him.
